item.title: Spacetech Startup Cosmoserve Nets $6 Mn, Eyes Commercialisation By 2028
item.dc:creator: Gaurav Bagur
item.description: Cosmoserve Space has raised $6 Mn in a seed funding round led by Japan-based Rebright Partners. While Aranya Holdings and…
item.content:encoded:
Cosmoserve Space has raised $6 Mn in a seed funding round led by Japan-based Rebright Partners. While Aranya Holdings and Naandi Ventures also participated in the round, existing investors AUM Ventures and Shakti VC doubled down on their erstwhile bet. 

The startup shared plans to utilise the fresh capital to support tech demonstrations, fuel two upcoming missions, as well enhance the operations of its recently unveiled Hyderabad facility. 

Cosmoserve has now raised over $9 Mn since inception last year. The startup has doubled its valuation since it raised pre-seed funding in September, founder Chiranjeevi Phanindra told Inc42. The exact valuation is yet to be discerned. 

For context, the startup is building tech to remove defunct satellites and orbital debris from space and reduce the collision risks for operational spacecraft in a cost effective manner. 

It plans on optimising costs by setting up features within its craft that will allow it to refuel in-orbit and remove multiple pieces of debris in a single mission. 

The startup made its first tech demonstration, Mission Embrace-1, aboard Skyroot Aerospace’s Vikram-1 rocket. The mission was designed to test the startup’s soft robotic capture system that removes space debris, but the system’s robotic petals failed to deploy as intended. 

Cosmoserve claims to have now identified and addressed potential issues with the thermal mechanism used to release the petals and the impact of low temperatures on the system, according to Phanindra. 

The startup is now gearing up for Embrace-2, an upgraded version of the mission to validate its upgraded robotic capture mechanism, which is expected to launch in the coming months. It is also planning a full-scale demonstration of its debris-removal capabilities, aiming to break a world record by approaching within 10 m of a dead satellite. 

Phanindra, who served close to 15 years with the ISRO before setting up Cosmoserve in June 2025, believes that the startup would be able to complete all tech demos by 2027 and start commercial operations by 2028.

“We have several letters of intent from satellite constellation operators – one from the US, one from Europe and two from India. They have to abide by the regulation for removing the dead satellite from space … so we are aiming to get one paid customer before actual commercial operations begin,” he added. 

Cosmoserve’s Base 1

Alongside the funding announcement, Cosmoserve inaugurated its new space debris removal facility in Hyderabad named Base 1 today, in an event attended by union minister of state Dr Jitendra Singh and Telangana IT Minister D Sridhar Babu. 

Phanindra says that Base 1 is India’s first private and the world’s sixth facility equipped with space vision effects and microgravity simulation.

In simpler terms, Base 1 can recreate conditions that spacecraft and equipment encounter in space, allowing companies to test how their tech will perform before an actual mission. This includes simulating how objects behave in microgravity (near-weightlessness) and how they appear or function under space-like visual conditions.

This costs around ₹6 Cr to construct, per Phanindra. 

Base 1 houses infrastructure for designing, building and testing satellite servicing and space debris recovery missions. This includes an orbital rendezvous and capture lab, an ISO Class 8 clean room for satellite integration, a mission control centre and a microgravity simulation platform.

The facility will also support the development of in-orbit satellite repair and refuelling technologies. 

Besides, the startup plans to use Base 1 to develop more critical technologies in-house in order to increase its share of local manufacturing from 60% and reduce dependence on imported components such as optics, avionics and space-grade electronics. 

“Primarily, the core technology we are building is a soft robotic capture system. We have a space robotics innovation lab where the R&D is happening. Then the next technology we are working on is a vision-based navigation system,” the founder told Inc42.

item.title: Sarvam’s Prism Enters India’s Growing AI Decision Model Race
item.dc:creator: Ankush Das
item.description: AI models are increasingly being built to do more than answer questions. Some are now designed to make specific decisions,…
item.content:encoded:
AI models are increasingly being built to do more than answer questions. Some are now designed to make specific decisions, such as whether a customer query should go to a sales or support team, whether a document needs further review, or whether an AI agent has completed a task correctly.

In India, Kerala-based ConvAI Innovations was one of the first to explore this category with Laya, an open-weight decision model intended to run locally on devices such as laptops and phones. Hyderabad-based PurpleTalk’s research lab, Sthānika AI, has also developed Sieve, a family of decision models that returns probabilities for a fixed set of possible answers. 

Both startups are betting that specialised models can make these decisions faster and more efficiently than general-purpose AI systems. 

The space has now attracted Sarvam AI, one of India’s prominent homegrown AI model developers. The company introduced Prism, a decision model built on its 105B-parameter foundation model. Sarvam says Prism combines high accuracy with low response times, while allowing enterprises to customise and run it on their own infrastructure.

The launch raises a bigger question for India’s AI ecosystem, especially given the implications on cost, reliability and speed: Are decision models the opportunity for Indian AI startups to compete with global players, rather than trying to match them across every general-purpose AI capability?

What Are Decision Models, And Why Now?

Most large language models (LLMs) are designed to generate text. Even when asked to make a simple choice, they typically produce a response that another software system must interpret. This can add processing time, increase costs and introduce inconsistencies.

Decision models approach the problem differently. They receive information, a question and a defined set of possible answers, then return a score or probability for each option. Instead of generating a paragraph explaining which department should handle a customer complaint, for instance, the model can assign probabilities to sales, support and billing.

This makes them useful for repetitive tasks performed at scale, including customer-support routing, content moderation, fraud checks, security screening and evaluating the actions of AI agents. General-purpose models can perform these tasks too, but a specialised decision model may be faster and easier to integrate into workflows that require predictable outputs.

The category gained visibility with Jev, the first public model from TypeSafe AI. Global companies, including Microsoft and Perplexity, have since introduced their own decision-model offerings. Indian startups are also developing alternatives, with different priorities around local deployment, openness and enterprise use.

How Sarvam Is Positioning Prism

Prism is built on Sarvam 105B, the company’s large language model, but is fine-tuned specifically for making decisions. Rather than generating a sequence of words to arrive at an answer, it evaluates the available options in a single processing pass and returns a probability for each.

According to Sarvam, Prism recorded an average score of 71.8 across three evaluation indices, with a median response time of 44 milliseconds on an Nvidia B200 GPU. The company said this was the highest average score among the 25 decision models it tested that responded in under 100 milliseconds.

Sarvam also tested whether the order of available options would change the model’s decision. It reported that Prism produced consistent results across 2,000 questions after applying a fixed ordering mechanism before scoring. The company further said that Prism’s observed error rates were lower than its predicted error rates across the confidence thresholds it tested, including in Indian languages.

These are company-reported results, and independent testing across comparable workloads will be important to establish how they translate into production performance.

Sarvam is releasing Prism’s weights under the Apache 2.0 licence. This allows developers to access the model’s trained parameters, adapt them and deploy the model on their own infrastructure, subject to the licence terms. It is also available through an API.

The company is targeting applications such as customer-support routing, document intelligence, security checks, prompt-injection detection and evaluation of AI-agent activity. Its positioning is not simply about offering another language model, but about adding a specialised decision-making component to the broader AI stack.

India’s Decision Model Race Heats Up

Laya, Sieve and Prism reflect different approaches to decision models in India. Laya prioritises small models that can run locally, while PurpleTalk’s research lab Sthānika AI focuses on open-weight Sieve models, with an emphasis on evaluation and tasks such as intent detection and AI-agent tool selection. Sarvam’s Prism builds on its foundation-model capabilities, with speed, confidence calibration, Indian-language performance and open-weight deployment among its key selling points.

Articul8, an enterprise AI company, is also developing the category through Bivia, its multimodal decision model designed for domain-specific, evidence-backed decisions across text, images, documents, audio and video. 

Ananthanarayanan S, managing director for India at Articul8, said Sarvam’s launch adds to the growing range of general-purpose models, while positioning Bivia around a different enterprise need. He said Articul8 benchmarks Bivia against models such as Jev and evaluates it through a broader enterprise lens, including its ability to abstain when evidence is insufficient.

He believes that the competition, however, will extend beyond benchmark scores and response times. Enterprises need models that can handle unfamiliar situations reliably and integrate with existing systems through domain grounding, orchestration and execution frameworks. 

Prism has also drawn scrutiny from developers and independent evaluators. Sandipan Kundu, a developer relations and AI engineer focused on fine-tuning and inference, and the builder of Tensorant, a platform for fine-tuning, evaluating and deploying open models, said on X that the model appeared capable but questioned whether its 44-millisecond median latency claim reflected real-world performance. He cited a p95 latency of 420 milliseconds in his testing. He also flagged the cost of self-hosting a model of its size. 

Separately, Faizan Shaik, a software engineer at Atlan, an enterprise data and metadata management platform, shared results from the company’s Decision Bench, where Prism scored 91.5% across 1,071 decisions on 36 public datasets, placing it 12th among 22 models. His evaluation reported a median latency of 65 milliseconds on a B200 GPU. These assessments suggest that Prism is competitive, but also underline the need to examine performance across different benchmarks and deployment conditions.

For Indian builders, the opportunity lies in proving that specialised decision models can deliver measurable gains in cost, latency and reliability across real-world workflows.

[Edited by: Nikhil Subramaniam]

item.title: Daksham Capital Launches ₹300 Cr Consumer Fund, Marks First Close At ₹125 Cr
item.dc:creator: Shrishti Bisht
item.description: Multi-family office and wealth management group Daksham Capital has launched its maiden consumer-focused fund, Daksham Growth Ventures (DGV) Fund I,…
item.content:encoded:
Multi-family office and wealth management group Daksham Capital has launched its maiden consumer-focused fund, Daksham Growth Ventures (DGV) Fund I, with a target corpus of ₹150 Cr and a ₹150 Cr greenshoe option. 

The fund has secured around ₹125 Cr in its first close, following its registration as a SEBI Category II AIF last month.

Family offices, high-net-worth individuals (HNIs), ultra-high-net-worth individuals (UHNIs), and entrepreneurs participated in the first close. The fund will continue raising capital towards its target, including the greenshoe option.

Led by cofounder and managing partner Shivam Diwan, DGV plans to invest in 10-15 startups, with cheques ranging from ₹5 Cr to ₹20 Cr. It will primarily back Pre-Series A and Series A startups, while considering select later-stage investments.

Its investment mandate spans D2C brands, consumer enablers, B2B2C platforms, supply-chain businesses, and startups using AI in consumer services.

Betting On Capital Efficiency

DGV will focus on businesses with established product-market fit rather than those still testing demand, Diwan told Inc42.

“We will only come where the product-market-fit risk is established,” he said.

The fund will typically evaluate startups with annual recurring revenue (ARR) of ₹25-75 Cr, assessing their unit economics, addressable market, founders’ execution capabilities, and differentiation. It is targeting businesses with the potential to scale annual revenue to ₹300-500 Cr.

Startups need not be profitable when DGV invests, but the fund expects them to have positive or neutral contribution margins, even if they remain loss-making at the EBITDA level.

“Growth by burning an enormous amount of money is not the mantra. It should be a capital-efficient business,” Diwan said.

Beyond capital, DGV plans to help portfolio startups with corporate governance, financial reporting, brand positioning, leadership development, and distribution expansion. It also intends to provide board-level guidance and access to its industry network.

The fund will evaluate businesses across food and beverages, apparel, snacking, beauty and personal care, accessories, jewellery, and bags.

Direct consumer businesses are expected to account for 50-70% of its investments. The remainder will go towards consumer enablers, including contract manufacturers, sourcing and supply chain companies, and B2B2C platforms.

DGV is also open to businesses outside the traditional consumer sector, provided their growth is linked to consumer demand.

Diwan said the fund is evaluating startups across food and beverages, accessories, and B2B2C segments, including a few D2C brands. It is yet to make an investment. 

DGV will also consider a small number of late-stage investments in startups that could go public within two to three years. These deals are likely to comprise largely secondary transactions, Diwan said.

Bullish On Consumer AI And Enablers

DGV expects AI to play a growing role in consumer businesses over the next decade, particularly in product discovery, personalisation, customer acquisition, and fulfilment.

While it does not intend to invest directly in deeptech or standalone AI startups, the fund will evaluate consumer businesses using AI to improve customer engagement and operations.

Diwan expects consumer AI to gain momentum over the next 12-24 months, with startups increasingly integrating the technology into how consumers discover, evaluate, and purchase products.

The fund is also bullish on consumer enablers, particularly contract manufacturers and B2B businesses supplying multiple brands. Diwan said these businesses offer exposure to demand across several brands, reducing dependence on a single consumer-facing startup.

Daksham’s launch adds to the pool of dedicated capital targeting Indian consumer businesses. Earlier this year, Kairon Capital announced the ₹90 Cr first close of its maiden consumer-focused fund against a ₹150 Cr target and a ₹50 Cr greenshoe option.

Fireside Ventures closed its fourth fund at ₹2,265 Cr ($253 Mn) in December last year. The fund aims to invest in 30-35 early-stage consumer brands, with initial cheques of $1 Mn to $12 Mn, across categories including health and wellness, food and beverages, beauty and personal care, and lifestyle.

item.title: CERT-In Flags AI-Driven Cyberattacks On Indian BFSI
item.dc:creator: Anne Florentyna
item.description: India’s cybersecurity watchdog CERT-In has issued a critical warning to entities in the banking, financial services and insurance (BFSI) sector…
item.content:encoded:
India’s cybersecurity watchdog CERT-In has issued a critical warning to entities in the banking, financial services and insurance (BFSI) sector over an escalating campaign of AI-driven cyberattacks targeting payment and disbursement APIs.

In an advisory dated November 4, 2026, the Indian Computer Emergency Response Team (CERT-In) identified the threat actor behind the campaign as ‘CRAFTY FALCON’, describing it as an AI-assisted financial threat actor that uses machine intelligence to identify targets, execute attacks at machine speed and exploit victims’ own payment and disbursement APIs to initiate unauthorised fund transfers.

Banks, non-banking financial companies (NBFCs), fintech companies and other financial services entities have been warned of the growing threat.

CERT-In’s Computer Security Incident Response Team-Finance (CSIRT-Fin) said the campaign has witnessed a significant escalation, with successful attacks continuing to be reported across the financial services ecosystem. The agency has urged all BFSI entities to treat the campaign as an immediate and continuing threat.

Repeat Attacks Despite Remediation

A key concern highlighted in the advisory is the threat actor’s continued targeting of financial entities that had already received earlier restricted advisories and undertaken remediation measures.

According to CERT-In, some of these organisations have been deliberately targeted again, including cases where remediation was incomplete. The attacks have also been timed to coincide with holidays, weekends and other periods of reduced monitoring, potentially delaying detection and response.

CERT-In’s analysis identified the use of multiple publicly available AI-driven offensive security tools in the campaign. These include the ARTEX family of large language model (LLM)-based tools, PentAGI, an autonomous multi-agent AI penetration testing system, and the Cairn attack search engine, alongside the CyberStrikeAI framework.

These tools can execute complete attack chains autonomously, generate and refine large volumes of customised attack scripts in rapid succession, and adapt their payloads based on responses from targeted systems.

The supporting attack infrastructure also changes frequently, with IP addresses rotating within hours to days. CERT-In said infrastructure fingerprints and detailed detection rules have been shared with affected entities through restricted advisories.

AI Agents Pose Growing Cybersecurity Risks

The latest advisory follows another critical warning issued by CERT-In in October, when the agency flagged attackers using publicly available agentic AI tools to conduct financially motivated intrusions into Indian organisations.

The watchdog warned that autonomous AI agents, ostensibly deployed for research and evaluation, had accessed live systems without authorisation, reading business records containing personal data and confidential information.

Meanwhile, the Indian Cyber Crime Coordination Centre (I4C) has also warned banks, NBFCs and fintech startups about the growing use of AI agents by cybercriminals to perpetrate financial fraud.

The agency said it had uncovered multiple individual cases in which malicious agentic AI systems exploited compromised financial systems to execute unauthorised transactions involving amounts running into crores of rupees.

CERT-In Flags Vulnerabilities In Tata Motors’ Connected Vehicle Apps

Separately, CERT-In has flagged multiple vulnerabilities in select versions of Tata Motors’ iRA 2.0 and iRA.ev connected vehicle applications, which could allow attackers to access sensitive credentials and vehicle-related information.

The agency identified four vulnerabilities, including hardcoded service account credentials, API keys and authorisation tokens within the applications; inadequate validation of URLs and origins loaded through the apps’ WebView component; authentication tokens being recorded in application logs; and improper implementation of SSL certificate pinning in the network security configuration.

CERT-In has urged users to update their applications to the latest versions of iRA 2.0 (version 26.8.2) and iRA.ev (version 26.9.1).

The applications provide access to connected vehicle functionalities, including vehicle status updates, health monitoring, trip details and remote vehicle commands.

item.content:encoded:
Ecommerce enablement platform Shiprocket turned profitable in the September quarter, reporting a consolidated net profit of ₹0.6 Cr against a net loss of ₹20.3 Cr in Q2 FY26.

Operating revenue rose 34.7% to ₹673.6 Cr during the quarter under review from ₹500.2 Cr a year ago.

Shiprocket, which listed on the NSE and BSE in August, had posted a net loss of ₹13.7 Cr in Q1 FY27. Sequentially, operating revenue increased 13.8% from ₹592.1 Cr.

Shiprocket’s revenue grew faster than its expenditure during the quarter. Total expenses increased 29.6% to ₹692.9 Cr from ₹534.8 Cr.

Other income increased to ₹19.9 Cr from ₹14.3 Cr, taking total income to ₹693.5 Cr, marginally above total expenses. The company reported no tax expense for the quarter.

item.title: Tonbo Imaging Turns Profitable In Q2 With ₹23.5 Cr PAT
item.dc:creator: Palak Sharma
item.description: Defence tech company Tonbo Imaging swung to a consolidated net profit of ₹23.5 Cr in the September quarter of FY27…
item.content:encoded:
Defence tech company Tonbo Imaging swung to a consolidated net profit of ₹23.5 Cr in the September quarter of FY27 from a net loss of ₹9.6 Cr in the year-ago period, supported by a sharp jump in operating revenue.

The Bengaluru-based company’s revenue from operations surged 1,963.3% YoY to ₹183.3 Cr during the quarter under review from ₹8.9 Cr in Q2 FY26. 

Sequentially, Tonbo returned to the black from a net loss of ₹17.7 Cr in Q1 FY27. Operating revenue rose 409% from ₹36 Cr in the preceding quarter.

Tonbo develops imaging and sensor systems for defence applications, including surveillance, reconnaissance, and targeting. Its products include thermal imaging systems, weapon sights, handheld thermal imaging binoculars, fire-control systems, and missile seekers. 

Tonbo’s total expenses rose 610.5% to ₹153.7 Cr in Q2 FY27 from ₹21.6 Cr in the corresponding quarter last year.

Despite the increase in spending, the revenue surge helped Tonbo post a profit before tax of ₹31.4 Cr against a pre-tax loss of ₹10.7 Cr in Q2 FY26.

Other income declined to ₹1.9 Cr from ₹2 Cr a year ago, taking total income to ₹185.2 Cr.

item.dc:creator: Vinaykumar Rai

item.content:encoded:
Shares of omnichannel eyewear retailer Lenskart surged as much as 11.1% to an all-time high of ₹767.4 on the BSE today after the company reported a sharp increase in its September-quarter profit.

The stock opened 7.8% higher at ₹745.05 against yesterday’s closing price of ₹691. It subsequently pared some gains to trade at ₹733.55 at 11:15 IST, up 6.2%. At that price, Lenskart’s market capitalisation stood at ₹1,27,586.8 Cr (about $13.5 Bn).

The rally followed Lenskart’s Q2 FY27 results, announced yesterday. Consolidated net profit increased 124.7% YoY to ₹232.5 Cr, while operating revenue grew 35.7% to ₹2,845 Cr. Revenue growth outpaced the increase in expenses, supporting the improvement in profitability.

Most brokerages remained positive on the company, pointing to strong same-store sales growth in India, store additions, higher realisations, and increasing in-house manufacturing.

Brokerages Back Growth Outlook

Jefferies retained its ‘Buy’ rating and raised its price target to ₹780 from ₹680, citing continued growth and margin expansion.

The brokerage said Lenskart is broadening its customer base through Hustlr Club, targeting the next 100 Mn Indians, while its premium retail format, evolv, and smart glasses offer additional growth opportunities. It added that strong growth supports the company’s premium valuation.

Equirus also raised its target to ₹874 for December 2027 from ₹698 for September 2027, retaining its ‘Long’ rating.

The brokerage expects Lenskart’s revenue to grow at a compounded annual rate of 24% between FY26 and FY29, supported by growth in both India and international markets. It models around 620 annual store additions over the next few years and expects greater in-house manufacturing to support margins.

Nomura retained a ‘Buy’ rating with a target of ₹888, implying potential upside of 21.1% from ₹733.55. It highlighted operating leverage across India and international operations, with in-house manufacturing and rent leverage supporting domestic margins.

Meanwhile, CLSA maintained an ‘Outperform’ rating with a ₹773 target. It said Q2 sales growth was in line with its estimate, while EBITDA exceeded consensus estimates by 3%. The brokerage highlighted robust India volumes and better-than-expected profitability.

Manufacturing Supports Margin Outlook

HSBC retained its ‘Buy’ rating with a ₹790 target, highlighting India same-store sales growth of around 21% and international constant-currency growth of 23%. The brokerage sees a larger opportunity in international operations than previously anticipated and revised its assessment of India’s margin expansion potential.

Macquarie maintained an ‘Outperform’ rating with a ₹750 target. It said faster store additions and an improved product mix helped India EBITDA grow 50% YoY, exceeding its expectations.

The brokerage also sees AI-led eye testing increasing testing capacity and easing constraints arising from optometrist availability. It factored in stronger average selling prices, supported by 7% growth in the first half of FY27.

Lenskart added 165 net stores during Q2, including 143 in India and 22 overseas. India same-store sales grew 20.8%, while eyewear volumes increased 26.5% to 86 Lakh units. 

Citi took a more cautious stance, retaining its ‘Neutral’ rating despite raising its target to ₹700 from ₹650.

While store expansion, premium lenses, and higher volumes should support growth, the brokerage expects operating leverage and in-house manufacturing to drive gradual margin improvement.

However, it said premium valuations and tougher comparisons in the second half would limit the scope for a valuation rerating.

item.title: Centre Weighs Withdrawing Safe Harbour For Meta, Google, X: Report
item.dc:creator: Shrishti Bisht
item.description: The Centre is exploring withdrawing safe harbour protection from social media platforms such as Facebook, Instagram, YouTube, and X, potentially…
item.content:encoded:
The Centre is exploring withdrawing safe harbour protection from social media platforms such as Facebook, Instagram, YouTube, and X, potentially exposing them to legal liability for content posted by their users.

The Ministry of Electronics and Information Technology (MeitY) has begun discussions on whether these platforms should continue to enjoy protection under Section 79 of the Information Technology (IT) Act, 2000, The Indian Express reported.

The government is examining whether the protection should be restricted to services that merely transmit information, including internet service providers (ISPs), telecom service providers (TSPs), and peer-to-peer messaging platforms.

However, discussions remain exploratory, and no final decision has been taken. Withdrawing the protection from social media platforms would likely require amendments to the IT Act and parliamentary approval, the report said.

Algorithms Under Scrutiny 

The move comes amid growing scrutiny of social media platforms over harmful content, child safety and the role of recommendation algorithms in determining what users see online.

Meanwhile, the Supreme Court has sought responses from the Centre and Meta on a PIL seeking a regulatory framework to protect children from algorithmic addiction and online harms.

The petition, filed by Sreerupa Chowdhury, alleged that platforms such as Facebook, Instagram and WhatsApp use features such as infinite scrolling, autoplay videos and push notifications to encourage compulsive use.

It also raised concerns over inadequate age-verification mechanisms, online grooming and the circulation of child sexual abuse material (CSAM).

The SC separately questioned whether existing legal protections are adequate to address the circulation of child sexual exploitation and abuse material on social media platforms.

In its October 15 order in the Just Rights for Children Alliance vs S Harish case, the SC called for a separate framework of penalties, including monetary fines, for social media companies that fail to comply with the law. It said the withdrawal of safe harbour should be reserved for serious violations.

Safe harbour protects internet intermediaries from being held liable for content posted by their users, subject to certain conditions. This has allowed social media platforms to host user-generated content without being legally responsible for every post, video or comment.

However, the government is questioning whether platforms can still be considered passive intermediaries when their algorithms decide what content users see and how widely it is circulated.

The discussions have also been shaped by concerns over the role of social media in public discourse, including during the students’ protests in July, when Instagram became a key platform for mobilising support.

Relations between the government and social media companies have come under further strain in recent months. In July, the IT Ministry summoned Meta’s global policy executives after Facebook briefly withheld a video uploaded by Prime Minister Narendra Modi during the protests. The Centre has also raised concerns over deepfakes and compliance with Indian laws.

The latest discussions follow reports in September that Meta could lose its intermediary status in India, potentially affecting the safe harbour protection available to Facebook, Instagram and WhatsApp.

The Parliamentary Standing Committee on Communications and Information Technology has also called for stronger action against social media companies. Any move to withdraw safe harbour protection, however, is likely to face opposition from the technology industry and civil society organisations.

item.title: SaaS Company Amagi’s Q2 Profit Jumps Nearly 30X To ₹74.8 Cr
item.dc:creator: Palak Sharma
item.description: Listed media SaaS company Amagi reported a nearly 30X YoY jump in its consolidated net profit to ₹74.8 Cr in…
item.content:encoded:
Listed media SaaS company Amagi reported a nearly 30X YoY jump in its consolidated net profit to ₹74.8 Cr in the September quarter (Q2 FY27), as revenue growth outpaced expenses.

The company had posted a net profit of ₹2.5 Cr in the year-ago quarter. Sequentially, profit rose 120.7% from ₹33.9 Cr.

Operating revenue increased 27% to ₹475.8 Cr from ₹374.8 Cr in Q2 FY26. It grew 8.9% from ₹436.9 Cr in the preceding quarter.

Amagi provides cloud software that helps media companies produce, distribute, and monetise television and streaming content. 

Including other income, its total income stood at ₹501.9 Cr in Q2 FY27 as against ₹389.6 Cr a year ago and ₹454.5 Cr in Q1 FY27.

Amagi’s total expenses increased 9% to ₹419.3 Cr from ₹384.5 Cr.

Alongside the results, Amagi’s board approved the appointment of former Accenture chief strategy and innovation officer Bhaskar Ghosh as an additional non-executive independent director for three years.

It also approved the appointment of promoter and CTO Srividhya Srinivasan as a whole-time director for five years. She will retain her CTO designation. Listed media SaaS company Amagi reported a nearly 30X YoY jump in its consolidated net profit to ₹74.8 Cr in the September quarter (Q2 FY27), driven by revenue growth outpacing expenses, lower ESOP-related costs, and a lower effective tax rate.

The company had posted a net profit of ₹2.5 Cr in the year-ago quarter. Sequentially, profit rose 120.7% from ₹33.9 Cr.

Operating revenue increased 27% to ₹475.8 Cr from ₹374.8 Cr in Q2 FY26. It grew 8.9% from ₹436.9 Cr in the preceding quarter.

Amagi provides cloud software that helps media companies launch, manage, distribute, and monetise television and streaming content.

Including other income, its total income stood at ₹501.9 Cr compared with ₹389.6 Cr a year ago and ₹454.5 Cr in Q1 FY27. Total expenses increased 9% to ₹419.3 Cr from ₹384.5 Cr.

Adjusted EBITDA grew 114% to ₹89.1 Cr, with its margin expanding 7.6 percentage points to 18.7%.

The company said ESOP-related costs declined to ₹25.4 Cr from ₹45 Cr a year ago. Its effective tax rate fell to 9.4% from 50%, with carried-forward losses in India offsetting a growing share of its profit base.

Meanwhile, other income rose 75.7% to ₹26.1 Cr, primarily driven by returns on IPO proceeds invested in fixed deposits and mutual funds.

However, Amagi said Q2 margins also benefited from the timing of planned senior hires, with some associated costs expected in subsequent quarters. It described its first-half adjusted EBITDA margin of 15.3% as a more representative near-term baseline.

Amagi’s Revenue Mix

Amagi generates revenue from three business verticals — streaming unification, monetisation and marketplace, and cloud modernisation.

Streaming unification, which helps media companies manage content distribution across streaming platforms, remained its largest vertical. Revenue grew 35% to ₹261.1 Cr, accounting for 54.9% of operating revenue.

The company attributed growth primarily to existing customers distributing channels across more streaming platforms.

Its monetisation and marketplace vertical, which helps content providers generate advertising revenue and expand distribution, reported revenue of ₹119.8 Cr, up 28%. It contributed 25.2% of operating revenue.

Growth was supported by higher monetised advertising impression volumes. Customer deployments also expanded the use of in-content advertising and tools that adapt ad breaks for different streaming platforms.

Meanwhile, cloud modernisation revenue rose 9% to ₹94.9 Cr, contributing 19.9% of operating revenue. The vertical helps broadcasters shift operations from on-premise infrastructure to cloud-based systems.

Amagi said growth in this vertical was affected by a higher year-ago base that included revenue recognised from a large broadcaster migration. Excluding this impact, the company said the vertical’s revenue would have grown about 36%.

Content And Advertising Growth

On the operational front, cumulative hours of content processed since inception increased 43% to 1 Mn. Channel deliveries grew 29% to 10,787, while its distributor network expanded 24% to 477.

Monetised advertising impressions increased 65% to 16 Bn during the quarter.

Amagi said its priorities for the remainder of FY27 remain sustaining revenue growth, improving operating leverage, and strengthening cash conversion. It plans to continue investing in AI capabilities, product development, people, and technology.

Alongside the results, its board approved the appointment of former Accenture chief strategy and innovation officer Bhaskar Ghosh as an additional non-executive independent director for three years, subject to shareholder approval.

It also approved the appointment of promoter and CTO Srividhya Srinivasan as a whole-time director for five years, subject to shareholder approval. She will retain her CTO designation.

item.content:encoded:
PhysicsWallah Back Among Profits

PhysicsWallah had a blockbuster Q2 FY27. The quarter saw the edtech giant swing back to profitability. With South India emerging as its next growth frontier and a NEET slowdown still lingering, can PW build on its Q2 momentum?

Here’s a quick glance at the edtech firm’s Q2 FY27 performance: 

  • Net profit more than doubled YoY to ₹143.6 Cr 
  • Operating revenue jumped 18.2% YoY to ₹1,242.3 Cr
  • Total expenses also rose nearly 11% YoY ₹1,105.4 Cr
  • EBITDA improved 52.6% YoY to ₹348 Cr

PW’s Growth Engines: The edtech major’s Q2 show was driven by healthy revenue growth, tighter cost control and improving operating leverage. Online business remained PW’s primary growth engine, while the offline network continued to add centres and enrolments. The company also benefited from a shift away from direct lending, reducing balance sheet risk. 

The startup’s next priority is its AI tutor (currently in pilot), which could reduce the cost of personalised learning and extend its reach beyond physical classrooms.

NEET Slowdown: The quarter was not without challenges. A delayed NEET exam cycle slowed enrolments and collections, impacting both online and offline verticals. To offset the gap, PW is launching full-length crash courses and increasing non-NEET enrolments. As a result, the management expects some collections to spill into the next quarter, while anticipating stronger recovery in the next academic session.

The Next Frontier: PW has now identified South India as its next major growth opportunity, which is home to a large student base. PW is pursuing the region through an online-first playbook rather than relying primarily on new physical centres. It also plans to tap into AI-led live translation to reach students across multiple Indic languages without adding significant academic cost. 

With profitability improving and AI becoming central to its strategy, here’s how PhysicsWallah fared on the financial front in Q2…

From The Editor’s Desk

Elo Elo Group Bags $80 Mn

  • Microdrama platform Story TV’s parent has raised nearly ₹756 Cr in its Series C round led by NBCUniversal and Hornbill Capital to invest in premium original content across Indian languages, expand globally and strengthen its AI capabilities.
  • Founded in 2020, EloElo Group’s portfolio spans four products. Story TV offers microdramas, while Master is a microlearning platform. It also sells AI-powered tools for creators and an AI companion agent called Voxy. It has raised $130 Mn to date.
  • Microdramas are gaining global popularity as they are specifically built for mobile-first users and rely heavily on high-octane storytelling. The global microdrama industry is projected to generate $14 Bn in revenue by 2026-end.

Razorpay All Set For IPO

  • The fintech major has received SEBI’s approval for its proposed IPO. The startup is now eyeing a listing between January and March 2027. This comes five months after Razorpay filed its IPO papers via the confidential route in June.
  • The ₹5,000 Cr to ₹6,000 Cr public issue is expected to value the company at around ₹47,300 Cr. The IPO will likely comprise both a fresh issue and an offer-for-sale component. 
  • Founded in 2014, Razorpay offers payment processing, business banking, payroll, and lending solutions. It has raised more than $800 Mn in funding to date from the likes of Y Combinator, Tiger Global Management, Ribbit Capital and Lightspeed.

NPCI Goes Beyond Payments

  • Moving beyond its mainstay, the National Payments Corporation of India has set up a new subsidiary, called NPCI Tech Solutions Ltd, to build capabilities in AI, blockchain, and digital financial infrastructure.
  • The payments body has appointed Vishal Kanvaty as the subsidiary’s MD and CEO. The new vertical will oversee GCC services, the Unified Ticketing Platform and other digital public infrastructure programmes.
  • The NTSL formation comes as advances in AI and other emerging technologies open up new opportunities across digital infrastructure and financial services. The subsidiary will pursue these opportunities and strengthen NPCI’s technology capabilities.

Nykaa’s Profitable Q2 Show

  • The beauty and fashion ecommerce major reported a 206.8% YoY jump in its net profit to ₹101.2 Cr in Q2 FY27. This came on the back of a stronger show by the beauty vertical and narrowing fashion losses.
  • Meanwhile, operating revenue also rose 28.1% YoY to ₹3,006 Cr in the quarter under review. EBITDA surged 65% YoY to ₹263 Cr. However, expenses also continued to bite and rose 24.8% YoY to ₹2,867.1 Cr in Q2 FY27.
  • On the operational front, Nykaa’s GMV grew 30% YoY to ₹6,151 Cr during the quarter. Meanwhile, its quick commerce offering, Nykaa Now, expanded to 15 cities in Q2 FY27. The company is targeting more than 25 cities by the end of FY27.

Mapping Agentic AI Liabilities

  • The Data Security Council of India has proposed a new framework to determine liability when AI agents cause harm. It has recommended that the responsibility of harm should be assigned based on each participant’s decisions and degree of control.
  • DSCI identifies 12 categories of potential harm, including privacy breaches, security threats, discrimination, safety risks, inaccurate outputs, IP violations, deepfakes, loss of control and AI-enabled cybercrime.
  • DSCI argues that accountability should be traced via decisions such as model selection, system configuration and human oversight. It also pitches six safeguards, including monitoring model behaviour, restricting permissions and deploying scoped kill switches.

Inc42 Markets

Inc42 Startup Spotlight

How Karta Is Automating Customer Service For Banks

Most voice bots can answer questions. But banking calls often require action, be it checking loan status, retrieving documents or updating records. Karta AI is building voice agents that can resolve these complex financial calls end to end, thereby reducing queues and support costs.

Built For Banks: Founded in 2024, Karta operates an omnichannel customer communication platform spanning voice AI, chat, email and WhatsApp. Its AI agents use a predictive context engine that draws on knowledge bases, past interactions and live data to execute workflows across enterprise systems. 

This allows the startup to handle multiple customer intents in a single conversation rather than routing callers through multiple agents. 

Healthy Early Traction: The startup claims to handle around 20 Lakh user conversations every month across 25+ languages. Karta claims that its inbound servicing agent resolves about 70% of borrower queries and cuts cost per query by nearly 50%. The Bengaluru-based startup also claims to have 10-12 paying customers, including the likes of PhonePe, Pine Labs, Bajaj and Aavas. 

Eye On The Prize: Going forward, Karta plans to strengthen its end-to-end automation and multilingual capabilities, expand BFSI deployments, and grow its engineering and GTM teams. The startup’s challenge will be maintaining accuracy, security and compliance as it handles increasingly sensitive financial workflows. 

With India’s conversational AI market projected to become a $3.7 Bn opportunity by 2033, can Karta make voice agents the default layer for BFSI customer service?

item.title: Cleantech Startup altM Raises $10.3 Mn To Scale Manufacturing
item.dc:creator: Shrishti Bisht
item.description: Cleantech startup altM has raised $10.3 Mn (₹97.5 Cr) in a Series A funding round led by new investors Rainmatter…
item.content:encoded:
Cleantech startup altM has raised $10.3 Mn (₹97.5 Cr) in a Series A funding round led by new investors Rainmatter and Mela Ventures. Existing investors Omnivore, Theia Ventures, Aureolis Ventures and Spectrum Impact also participated.

The Bengaluru-based startup plans to use the fresh capital to expand manufacturing, build its sales pipeline and continue investing in research and development (R&D). A large chunk of the funds will go towards setting up a 1,000-tonne-per-year commercial manufacturing facility by 2028.

“We have three large focus areas for the company today. In the short term, we want to start converting revenues and building our sales pipeline from the pilot plant. From a manufacturing perspective, a large chunk of our investment will go into building the next 1,000-tonne-per-year commercial plant,” cofounder and CEO Apoorv Garg told Inc42.

The startup will also continue developing alternative materials and biochemicals. It plans to expand its sales team following the funding round. “The major influx will be on sales,” Garg added.

Founded in 2022 by former Tesla executives Garg and Yugal Raj Jain, altM develops specialty chemicals and biomaterials from agricultural residue for industrial applications.

Its platform converts lignocellulosic biomass, including sugarcane bagasse, rice straw and other agricultural residues, into materials for use in beauty and personal care, textiles, industrial chemicals, construction, packaging and consumer goods.

The platform uses the major fractions of biomass, including cellulose, hemicellulose and lignin, to produce multiple products from a single feedstock, offering an alternative to fossil-derived raw materials.

The latest round comes nearly three years after altM raised $3.5 Mn in a seed round in 2023. Since then, the startup has built an integrated R&D and pilot manufacturing facility in Bengaluru, bringing laboratory research, demonstration manufacturing and pilot production under one roof.

It has expanded its laboratory footprint nearly 5X, commissioned a demonstration manufacturing facility and advanced six molecules to the demonstration stage, with three selected for pilot production.

The first products advancing towards commercialisation include a lignin-derived SPF booster for suncare, a cellulose-based rheology modifier and bio-derived ferulic acid for cosmetics and personal care formulations.

The startup is currently focused on the BPC segment, while its R&D pipeline spans construction, electronics, automotive, polymers and battery materials.

Garg said altM has completed the installation of its 70-tonne-per-year pilot plant in Bengaluru’s Electronic City and is preparing to begin commercial production.

“We have been installing it since late 2025 and finally finished the installation in 2026. It’s still in pre-production, and we’re getting the right certifications and validations to take it to production this month,” Garg said.

The startup expects to begin fulfilling purchase orders in the current quarter, with its first product launches planned for the following quarter. It currently works with nearly 30 BPC customers at different stages of product development, testing and commercialisation. Around 16-18 of them are in testing and active validation, Garg said.

altM’s process involves breaking down plant matter into core polymers and upgrading these fractions into chemicals. Garg said the startup has filed six patents in India covering its deconstruction technology and processes for upgrading individual molecules. It is working on a seventh patent and plans to file patents in international markets as well.

The startup has carried out more than 15,000 reactions at the laboratory stage and translated over 500 reactions to the demonstration stage. It has also reduced the time taken to develop new molecules from 12-15 months to under six months, Garg said.

Looking ahead, altM aims to sell out the capacity of its existing pilot plant by the first quarter of FY28. Over the next five years, it plans to expand its manufacturing capacity to 10,000 tonnes per year, with the potential to generate 100-200 Mn in annual revenue, depending on the molecules produced.

item.title: Mahadev Betting App Promoter Ravi Uppal Arrested In The UAE: Report
item.dc:creator: Team Inc42
item.description: Ravi Uppal, co-promoter of the Mahadev online betting app, has reportedly been arrested in the United Arab Emirates (UAE). Officials…
item.content:encoded:
Ravi Uppal, co-promoter of the Mahadev online betting app, has reportedly been arrested in the United Arab Emirates (UAE).

Officials told news agency PTI that authorities in Dubai arrested the 46-year-old on the basis of an Interpol Red Notice issued against him at the request of Indian investigating agencies. 

According to the report, the Central Bureau of Investigation (CBI) and the Enforcement Directorate are now working to extradite Uppal back to India.

This comes days after the extradition of fellow Mahadev app co-promoter Saurabh Chandrakar from Oman to India. A CBI team brought Chandrakar back after a court there permitted his extradition to India in connection with a money laundering case being investigated by the ED.

Subsequently, a special court in Raipur, earlier this week, granted eight custody of Chandrakar to the CBI.

Uppal’s arrest in the UAE marks a development in the ongoing ED probe into the betting platform. He was previously also detained in the UAE in 2023, but local investigating agencies reportedly subsequently found that he was in Australia.

Agencies have reportedly also claimed that Uppal obtained a passport from Vanuatu, an island nation in the South Pacific, just like Chandrakar.

The Mahadev Betting App Saga 

This comes nearly years after the Enforcement Directorate filed a chargesheet against Uppal in October 2023 in connection with the alleged Mahadev app betting scam. 

As per investigators, the platform operated from outside India through a network of franchised panels and branches, which enrolled users and facilitated illegal betting on cricket, football and other events.

A probe by CBI revealed that the betting proceeds were allegedly routed through mule bank accounts and transferred overseas through hawala channels. Part of the money was allegedly paid to public servants to allow the syndicate to operate without hindrance. 

ED estimates the proceeds of crime in the Mahadev betting app case at around ₹6,000 Cr. Its investigation has also examined alleged links to senior politicians and bureaucrats in Chhattisgarh.

In March, the directorate provisionally attached 20 properties with an estimated market value of nearly ₹1,700 Cr under the Prevention of Money Laundering Act (PMLA). These included 20 properties in Dubai and New Delhi, including villas and apartments.

The ED alleges that these properties were acquired using illegal betting proceeds and held through entities controlled by Chandrakar and his associates.

Overall, as of March, the ED has searched more than 175 locations, arrested 13 people, and attached or frozen assets worth around ₹4,336 Cr. 

The wider investigation has also examined alleged links involving EaseMyTrip cofounder Nishant Pitti and former Chhattisgarh chief minister Bhupesh Baghel. Both have denied wrongdoing.

item.title: Cabinet Clears ₹2,814 Cr Scheme To Boost Lithium & Nickel Processing
item.dc:creator: Team Inc42
item.description: With an eye on reducing dependence on imported critical minerals, the Union Cabinet has approved a scheme to set up…
item.content:encoded:
With an eye on reducing dependence on imported critical minerals, the Union Cabinet has approved a scheme to set up domestic lithium and nickel processing facilities in the country. 

Called the Capex Support Scheme to Promote Critical Mineral Processing, the programme has been approved with a financial outlay of ₹2,814 Cr over a period of five years from FY27 to FY31. 

The outlay will pave the way for setting up four plants, two each for lithium and nickel processing. In a statement, the government said that the units will process lithium and nickel ores or intermediary products into high-purity compounds. Cobalt is also expected to be recovered as a by-product of nickel production.

Under the scheme, beneficiaries will receive milestone-linked capital subsidies covering 30% of their eligible investment, subject to certain thresholds. For lithium processing, support will be capped at ₹500 Cr per beneficiary. However, each of the two proposed lithium plants should have a minimum capacity of 30 kilo-tonnes.

For nickel processing, the maximum support will be ₹900 Cr per beneficiary, with each plant required to have a minimum capacity of 50 kilo-tonnes.

The scheme focuses on processing, rather than mining alone. This strategy aims to retain more value within India by converting raw materials into compounds, which are required by downstream industries.

The government said that the resulting capacity would support use cases across electric mobility, battery energy storage systems (BESS), electronics, defence and speciality steel.

“The scheme aims to develop domestic processing capabilities in India to support value addition within the country, reduce import dependence, and develop (the) value chain… This will support critical sectors such as electric mobility, BESS, electronics, defence, speciality steel etc,” read an official statement.

The government also said that the applicants will be selected through a two-stage process. The first stage will assess technical qualifications, followed by financial bidding. The beneficiaries will be selected based on the least-cost criterion, meaning qualified seeking the lowest capital expenditure support will be chosen.

Afterwards, incentives will be disbursed in three tranches linked to specified milestones. With this, the government aims to tie payments to progress rather than providing the entire subsidy upfront.

Reducing India’s Export Exposure

Citing its rationale for approving the scheme, the government said that critical mineral processing remains concentrated in a small number of global locations. This, as per the Centre, has left supply chains exposed to geopolitical disruptions, price volatility and potential restrictions.

As of now, India remains 100% import-dependent for raw and refined forms of many critical minerals, including lithium, cobalt and nickel. These minerals are critical components for India’s clean energy transition, electric vehicles, electronics, and advanced manufacturing sectors. 

As such, the scheme intends to strengthen domestic value chains, curb imports and support decarbonisation initiatives. But the road ahead will be tricky and will also require beneficiaries to secure raw materials and processing capabilities.

This is the second such scheme approved by the Union Cabinet in the past year. In December 2025, the cabinet also cleared a ₹1,500 Cr incentive scheme to develop at least 270 kilotons of annual recycling capacity for critical minerals.

item.title: Cybersecurity Agency I4C Warns Banks & Fintechs Against AI-Led Cyberattacks
item.dc:creator: Gaurav Bagur
item.description: The Indian Cyber Crime Coordination Centre (I4C) has warned banks, non-banking financial companies (NBFCs) and fintech startups against the growing…
item.content:encoded:
The Indian Cyber Crime Coordination Centre (I4C) has warned banks, non-banking financial companies (NBFCs) and fintech startups against the growing trend of cyberattackers using AI agents for financial frauds. 

In an advisory issued on November 3, the National Cybercrime Threat Analysis Unit (NCTAU), under the I4C, flagged that attackers were exploiting unpatched software and misconfigured internet-facing servers to gain access to financial infrastructure. 

The cybersecurity agency also said that it has unearthed multiple “individual” cases, where malicious agentic AI systems were exploiting compromised financial systems to undertake unauthorised transactions running into crores of Rupees.

Describing the modus operandi of these AI-led cyberattacks, the agency noted that perpetrators exploit unpatched software to compromise banking systems. Customer-facing complaint interfaces can also serve as potential entry points, added I4C. 

Once inside, NCTAU noted that attackers potentially target automated fund disbursement systems and APIs used for payments and transfers. 

The agency added that these cyberattackers then route funds through mule accounts across different banks and quickly move to withdraw the proceeds of the crime via IMPS and NEFT. The perpetrators then delete records and hide their tracks so that investigation becomes difficult, added the NCTAU. 

As such, the agency has advised financial institutions to take the following measures: 

  • Implement CERT-In’s critical advisories “urgently” on payment and disbursement APIs as well as AI agents
  • Report cyber incidents to CERT-In within six hours, and to RBI as well in the cases of banks or NBFCs 
  • Test payment APIs and strengthen customer-facing infrastructure
  • Set transaction limits, verify beneficiary details and monitor sudden changes in transaction speeds, volumes and patterns 
  • Ensure KYC and approval checks are completed before funds are transferred
  • Improve coordination between security, transaction monitoring and IT teams 
  • Conduct authorised red-team exercises to test how quickly security and payment controls respond to machine-speed attacks

The warning highlights how AI is accelerating the threat of cyber fraud for financial services firms. At the Global Fintech Fest (GFF) 2026 in September, both Prime Minister Narendra Modi and RBI Governor Sanjay Malhotra had urged fintechs to bolster cybersecurity and strengthen consumer trust.

At the same event, National Payments Council of India (NPCI) MD and CEO Dilip Asbe had also called on banks and payments companies to invest in AI to combat cyber threats. 

In line with this, CERT-In had also issued a critical advisory last month, raising concerns over cyberattackers using publicly-available agentic AI tools for financially motivated intrusions into Indian entities. 

The advisory follows disclosures by global AI firms OpenAI and Anthropic about their agents taking unauthorised actions during internal cybersecurity evaluations.

item.title: Tracxn Q2 Loss Narrows 26% YoY To ₹4.1 Cr, Revenue Stays Flat
item.dc:creator: Debarghya Sil
item.description: Listed private market intelligence platform Tracxn Technologies reported a 25.8% decline in its net loss to ₹4.1 Cr in the…
item.content:encoded:
Listed private market intelligence platform Tracxn Technologies reported a 25.8% decline in its net loss to ₹4.1 Cr in the September quarter of FY27 (Q2 FY27) from ₹5.6 Cr, helped by a lower tax charge. Sequentially, its loss widened 37.1% from ₹3 Cr.

Operating revenue remained largely flat, rising 0.3% to ₹21.3 Cr from ₹21.2 Cr. The top line increased 1.1% from ₹21.1 Cr in the preceding quarter.

The narrower YoY net loss reflects a change in tax expenses. Tracxn incurred a ₹6.2 Cr tax charge in Q2 FY26, compared with a ₹52 Lakh tax credit in the quarter under review.

Before tax, the company swung to a loss of ₹4.6 Cr from a profit of ₹62.4 Lakh a year earlier. Its pre-tax loss stood at ₹2.8 Cr in Q1 FY27.

The Bengaluru-based company provides private-company data and software to venture capital firms, private equity firms, investment banks, and corporate teams.

Total income, including other income and gains, stood at ₹22.7 Cr, compared with ₹22.5 Cr in Q2 FY26 and ₹22.6 Cr in the preceding quarter.

Tracxn’s total expenses rose 25% YoY to ₹27.3 Cr from ₹21.9 Cr. Sequentially, expenses increased 7.7% from ₹25.4 Cr.

For the first half of FY27, operating revenue declined marginally to ₹42.4 Cr from ₹42.5 Cr in the corresponding period last fiscal.

Total expenses increased 21.7% YoY to ₹52.7 Cr from ₹43.3 Cr, while net loss widened 60.6% to ₹7.1 Cr from ₹4.4 Cr.

Tracxn reported a net cash outflow of ₹6 Cr from operating activities in H1 FY27, against an inflow of ₹1 Cr a year earlier.

India Growth Offsets Overseas Decline

India accounted for 53% of Tracxn’s Q2 FY27 revenue, with domestic revenue growing 6.9% sequentially to ₹11.3 Cr. The company said this represented an annualised growth run rate of nearly 30%.

International revenue declined 4.8% sequentially to ₹10 Cr, accounting for the remaining 47%.

Tracxn said investments in data and sales capabilities in India over the past two to three years were driving domestic growth. It is now making similar investments across its international business units, which it expects to support growth over the coming quarters.

Its strategy involves creating specialised teams for customer segments, expanding relevant datasets and product capabilities, and then scaling sales teams.

For instance, monthly new customer wins in its India investment banking business increased from nine to 13 during FY26 and reached 20 in Q1 FY27. It is targeting 30 monthly wins.

Tracxn plans to expand the sales team responsible for closing deals from 34 members in December 2025 to around 60 by December 2026. Of these planned positions, 56 had been filled by September.

Sales and marketing teams accounted for 30% of its total headcount in Q2 FY27, up from 25% a year earlier.

AI And Data Expansion

Tracxn has introduced Model Context Protocol (MCP) connectors that allow paid users to access its proprietary company intelligence through AI tools including ChatGPT, Claude, Gemini, and Cursor.

It has also introduced an AI assistant that lets users query its database in plain English, alongside ready-to-use investor agents for tasks including due diligence, competitive benchmarking, sector research, and startup scouting. More workflows are planned.

On data coverage, Tracxn said its database contained detailed financials for more than 7.5 Mn companies across over 20 countries, while its global legal entity database covered 66 Mn entities.

The company is also using Tracxn Lite, which offers limited platform access, to attract potential paying customers. It reported 3.49 Lakh cumulative sign-ups and 17.1 Mn organic visits during Q2 FY27.

Customer accounts increased 13% YoY to 2,419, while users grew 16% to 6,854.

Tracxn said it expects annual cost growth to moderate to low single digits after its current investment phase, supported by AI-led reductions in data production costs. It expects this to help it return to profitability.

item.title: Now, upGrad Files Insolvency Petition Against Bira91 Over ₹1.02 Cr Dues
item.dc:creator: Shrishti Bisht
item.description: upGrad has filed an insolvency petition against B9 Beverages Ltd, the maker of Bira91 beer, over alleged unpaid dues of…
item.content:encoded:
upGrad has filed an insolvency petition against B9 Beverages Ltd, the maker of Bira91 beer, over alleged unpaid dues of ₹1.02 Cr, adding to the financial and legal challenges facing the brewer.

The petition, filed under Section 9 of the Insolvency and Bankruptcy Code (IBC), 2016, was submitted to the Delhi bench of the NCLT on October 22, as per documents reviewed by Moneycontrol.

upGrad has named B9 Beverages as the corporate debtor and sought the initiation of the corporate insolvency resolution process (CIRP) to recover the outstanding amount.

The petition does not disclose the nature of services provided by upGrad to the beverage maker.

Inc42 has reached out to upGrad and Anicut Capital for a comment on the development. The story will be updated on receiving a response.

The filing comes amid mounting liabilities and creditor disputes at B9 Beverages, which is facing insolvency-related action from multiple creditors.

In September, the NCLT directed B9 Beverages and its creditors to explore a settlement through mediation in connection with multiple insolvency proceedings. The tribunal also restrained the brewer from disposing of its assets while discussions were underway.

The company has also faced action from glass manufacturer Hindusthan National Glass & Industries Ltd (HNGIL), which sought to recover ₹11.8 Cr in alleged unpaid dues.

HNGIL issued a demand notice under Section 8 of the IBC over customised glass bottles manufactured against confirmed purchase orders but allegedly not collected by the brewer. The glassmaker claimed that more than 51 Lakh bottles worth over ₹7 Cr remained stored at its facilities, despite it encashing bank guarantees worth ₹3.91 Cr.

The latest development comes as the startup attempts to restructure its business amid a prolonged financial crisis.

In July, founder Ankur Jain stepped down from the company’s board and relinquished executive control and ownership following a dispute with investors and lenders.

VC firm Anicut Capital, one of Bira’s key lenders, subsequently took control of Jain and his family’s stake in the company, as per reports. 

Anicut had extended loans to B9 Beverages between 2017 and 2022, secured against the promoter family’s stake.

The brewer is now expected to be recapitalised by existing investors and lenders under a revival plan aimed at clearing statutory, employee and vendor dues and restarting operations.

Founded by Jain in 2015, Bira 91 raised more than $200 Mn from investors. Its annual revenue crossed $100 Mn in FY23. Its shareholders include Peak XV Partners, Sofina and Japan-based Kirin Holdings. Anicut Capital and Hero Corporate Services’ family office are among its key lenders.

Its troubles began after it converted into a public company, triggering fresh excise approval requirements across multiple states. This disrupted the production and sales of the beer. The company subsequently wrote off inventory worth around ₹80 Cr and fell behind on vendor payments.

The company eventually paused its packaged beer business amid a prolonged funding crunch, mounting vendor liabilities and difficulties in meeting employee and statutory obligations.

The company reported a net loss of ₹748 Cr in FY24, with accumulated losses of ₹2,117.9 Cr. Its auditor also warned that current liabilities exceeded assets by ₹487 Cr as of March 2024.

Under Section 9 of the IBC, an operational creditor can approach the NCLT to initiate insolvency proceedings after serving a demand notice and meeting the prescribed statutory conditions.

However, filing a petition does not automatically trigger insolvency proceedings. The NCLT will examine the application to determine whether the requirements for admission have been met.

item.title: PhysicsWallah Returns To The Black In Q2, Posts A Profit of ₹143.6 Cr
item.dc:creator: Anne Florentyna
item.description: Edtech major PhysicsWallah (PW) reported a consolidated net profit of ₹143.6 Cr in the second quarter (Q2) of the fiscal…
item.content:encoded:
Edtech major PhysicsWallah (PW) reported a consolidated net profit of ₹143.6 Cr in the second quarter (Q2) of the fiscal year 2026-27 (FY27), up 106% from ₹69.7 Cr in the year-ago quarter. In contrast, the listed company had posted a loss of ₹88.3 Cr in the preceding quarter. 

Meanwhile, operating revenue rose 18.2% to ₹1,242.3 Cr in the quarter under review from ₹1,051.3 Cr in Q2 FY26. On a sequential basis, the company’s top line also jumped 18.3% from ₹1,050.3 Cr in Q1 FY27.

Including other income of ₹92.4 Cr, PhysicsWallah’s total income stood at ₹1,334.6 Cr in the quarter under review.

In line with the top line, PW’s total expenses also rose 10.6% to ₹1,105.4 Cr in Q2 FY27 as against ₹999.6 Cr in the year-ago quarter. Employee benefit expenses, its largest cost centre, also rose 10.4% to ₹522.4 Cr from ₹473.1 Cr in the year-ago period.

In its investor presentation, PW also noted that its EBITDA stood at ₹348 Cr in the quarter under review, up 52.6% from ₹228 Cr in Q2 FY26. Meanwhile, EBITDA margin improved to 28% from 21.7% in Q2 FY26.

During the quarter, Physicswallah also reported a profit of ₹1.3 Cr from discontinued operations. Its subsidiary Finz Finance discontinued its lending business and transferred its loan portfolio to Auxilo Finserve for ₹95.8 Cr in October this year.

PhysicsWallah’s Omnichannel Engine

The online business accounted for the biggest chunk of PW’s top line in Q2 FY27. The vertical generated a revenue of ₹693.5 Cr during the quarter, up 26.4% from ₹548.7 Cr in Q2 FY26.

On the other hand, the offline segment reported a revenue of ₹540.9 Cr, marking a 9% YoY increase from ₹496.1 Cr. 

On the operational front, the listed edtech major said that it operated 370 offline centres at the end of September 2026. Meanwhile, unique online enrolments grew 12.9% YoY to 15 Lakh in Q2 FY27.

However, the quarter was not without its challenges. During the earnings call, the management said that the delayed NEET exam cycle slowed enrolments and collections, impacting both online and offline verticals. However, the offline business was impacted more. PW now expects collections to spill into Q3 FY27, while anticipating stronger recovery in the next academic session.

Noting that NEET accounts for only about 15% of online revenue, the management noted that the hit from the subdued performance of the medical exam vertical was largely offset by other categories. To further offset the gap, PW said that it is increasing non-NEET enrolments as well as launching full-length crash courses and a 360-degree tracker product.

PW’s Next Growth Bet

In the earnings call, PhysicsWallah cofounder and CEO Alakh Pandey also said that the company plans to scale its presence in South India for its “next leg of growth”. 

The edtech major plans to deploy an online-first playbook, instead of offline, to carve a niche in the five Southern states that have a total addressable market (TAM) of 1.5 Cr students. The key lever for the company in the region will be AI-powered translation, which will look to make batches available in 12 Indic languages with the same “star teachers” and no incremental academic cost. 

As for its outlook, the edtech company maintained a 30% consolidated revenue growth guidance. The management also said that it is targeting 100% EBITDA growth at group-level and near break-even for the offline business in the ongoing fiscal year.

Separately, the company’s board also approved a proposal to acquire an additional 12.25% stake in Utkarsh Classes for ₹2.6 Lakh. This is part of PW’s multi-tranche acquisition plan to acquire the startup as detailed in its November 2025 prospectus. 

Once the deal goes through, PW’s stake in Utkarsh Classes will increase to 87.75% from 75.5% currently. 

As part of this, the board approved the fourth tranche of investment, through which the listed company will acquire 25,599 equity shares. PhysicsWallah’s board also gave its nod to replace the PAT-linked valuation mechanism, previously underlined in the agreement for the fourth tranche, with a mutually agreed fixed purchase consideration.

item.title: NPCI Expands Beyond Payments With AI, Blockchain-Focused Subsidiary
item.dc:creator: Vinaykumar Rai
item.description: The National Payments Corporation of India (NPCI) has set up a wholly owned subsidiary, NPCI Tech Solutions Ltd (NTSL), to…
item.content:encoded:
The National Payments Corporation of India (NPCI) has set up a wholly owned subsidiary, NPCI Tech Solutions Ltd (NTSL), to build capabilities in AI, blockchain, and digital financial infrastructure beyond its core payments mandate.

The retail payments operator has appointed Vishal Kanvaty, who has been associated with NPCI for nearly a decade, as the subsidiary’s MD and CEO.

NPCI said NTSL will serve as the group’s technology and innovation arm. Its remit will also include global capability centre (GCC) services and technology services for eKYC Setu, the Unified Ticketing Platform (UTP), and other digital public infrastructure (DPI) programmes.

According to NPCI, Kanvaty has led the development and commercialisation of several platforms that now fall within NTSL’s focus areas.

NPCI MD & CEO Dilip Asbe said advances in AI and other emerging technologies are opening up opportunities across digital infrastructure and financial services. The subsidiary has been established to pursue these opportunities and strengthen the group’s technology capabilities, he added.

NPCI did not disclose the subsidiary’s investment outlay, revenue targets, customer pipeline, or timelines for rolling out new services.

NPCI’s Emerging Technology Push

The formation follows a series of technology initiatives by NPCI. At the Global Fintech Fest in September, it launched AiNxt and AtOM, platforms aimed at helping enterprises build AI agents and automate workflows across the payments ecosystem. 

AiNxt enables enterprises to build, test, and deploy custom AI agents, while AtOM is designed to handle integration, change management, and partner onboarding across UPI, with digitally signed interactions providing audit trails. 

NPCI’s work in emerging technologies also includes a multi-year research partnership with IISc, announced in March 2024, covering AI and blockchain. The collaboration envisaged developing models and software prototypes, alongside workshops and training programmes. 

On the payments side, NPCI demonstrated an agentic AI framework for UPI at GFF 2025. The demonstration showed how user-authorised AI assistants could discover products, place orders, and complete payments within a single conversational flow. 

The new technology arm joins NPCI’s existing subsidiaries focused on international payments, bill payments, and BHIM. With NTSL, the group now has four wholly owned subsidiaries: NPCI International Payments Ltd (NIPL), NPCI Bharat BillPay Ltd (NBBL), NPCI BHIM Services Ltd (NBSL), and NTSL.

The expansion comes alongside continued growth in its flagship payments network. UPI processed a record 25.47 Bn transactions in October, up 5.8% MoM, while transaction value increased 7.4% to ₹31.53 Lakh Cr. Average daily transaction value crossed ₹1 Lakh Cr for the first time.

This came ahead of the proposed introduction of merchant discount rate (MDR) charges on select UPI payments. NPCI deferred the rollout, originally scheduled for October 15, until after Diwali, with a revised implementation date yet to be announced.

item.title: Nykaa’s Q2 Profit More Than Triples To ₹101 Cr, Revenue Up 28% YoY
item.dc:creator: Anjali Jain
item.description: Beauty and fashion ecommerce major Nykaa reported a 206.8% jump in its consolidated net profit to ₹101.2 Cr in the…
item.content:encoded:
Beauty and fashion ecommerce major Nykaa reported a 206.8% jump in its consolidated net profit to ₹101.2 Cr in the September quarter of FY27 (Q2 FY27) from ₹33 Cr in the year-ago period, helped by stronger beauty profitability and narrower fashion losses.

Operating revenue rose 28.1% to ₹3,006 Cr from ₹2,346 Cr in Q2 FY26. Sequentially, net profit increased 26.9% from ₹79.8 Cr, while operating revenue grew 8.1% from ₹2,782 Cr.

Total expenses increased 24.8% to ₹2,867.1 Cr from ₹2,297.6 Cr, growing slower than operating revenue.

Including other income of ₹9.5 Cr, total income stood at ₹3,015.6 Cr. Profit before tax increased to ₹148.5 Cr from ₹55.4 Cr a year earlier.

EBITDA surged 65% YoY to ₹263 Cr, while EBITDA margin expanded to 8.7% from 6.8% in Q2 FY26.

Nykaa’s gross merchandise value (GMV) grew 30% to ₹6,151 Cr during the quarter, while gross profit increased 31% to ₹1,382 Cr. Gross margin improved to 46% from 44.9% a year earlier.

Beauty Business Drives Growth

Nykaa’s beauty segment reported a 26.6% increase in revenue to ₹2,699.7 Cr from ₹2,131.9 Cr a year earlier. Its segment profit before exceptional items rose to ₹180.2 Cr from ₹105.4 Cr.

The beauty vertical’s net sales value (NSV) increased 28% YoY to ₹2,536 Cr, while GMV grew 25% to ₹4,454 Cr. EBITDA jumped 51% to ₹267 Cr.

Nykaa attributed the growth to new customer acquisition, repeat customer engagement, and its expanding retail presence. Monthly average unique visitors increased 30% to 54.1 Mn, while average order value rose 5% to ₹2,149.

The company added 14 beauty stores during the quarter, taking its network to 338 stores across 111 cities.

Nykaa also added more than 330 beauty brands over the past year. Recent launches included French beauty brand Yves Rocher, luxury haircare brand Oribe, and Korean skincare brand Mamonde.

Meanwhile, its quick commerce offering, Nykaa Now, expanded to 15 cities in Q2 FY27 from three in Q1 FY26. The company is targeting more than 25 cities by the end of FY27.

Fashion Business Narrows Losses

Nykaa’s fashion segment reported a 42.9% increase in revenue to ₹287.2 Cr from ₹201 Cr a year earlier. Its loss before exceptional items narrowed to ₹7.7 Cr from ₹21.4 Cr.

The fashion business’s GMV grew 42% YoY to ₹1,674 Cr, while NSV increased 47% to ₹509 Cr.

It reported EBITDA of ₹1 Cr, compared with an EBITDA loss of ₹12 Cr in Q2 FY26.

During the quarter, Nykaa launched Nykaa Fashion LUXE, a curated destination for international luxury brands and Indian designer labels. The platform also added more than 250 brands.

Separately, House of Nykaa, its portfolio of owned beauty and fashion brands, crossed an annualised GMV run rate of ₹4,000 Cr, up 40% YoY. Its annualised NSV exceeded ₹2,300 Cr, an increase of 36%.

Expanding Its Makeup Portfolio

Alongside its results, Nykaa’s board approved acquiring an 82% stake in Simply Nam for up to ₹33 Cr. The transaction is expected to close by December 31.

Founded by celebrity makeup artist Namrata Soni and venture studio Bozzil, Simply Nam sells premium makeup products designed for Indian skin tones, climates, and everyday routines, according to the company.

Its FY26 turnover increased about 77% to ₹17 Cr from ₹9.6 Cr in FY25.

Following the acquisition, Soni will continue as cofounder and chief product officer, overseeing the brand’s creative direction, product development, and education initiatives.

The proposed acquisition will add a professional makeup brand to Nykaa’s colour cosmetics portfolio, which includes Nykaa Cosmetics and Kay Beauty.

In September, Nykaa also partnered with BOLD, L’Oreal’s corporate venture capital fund, to jointly invest in Indian beauty and personal care brands, combining its retail and distribution network with L’Oreal’s expertise and mentorship.

item.title: Lenskart Q2 Profit Jumps 125% YoY To ₹233 Cr, Revenue Rises 36%
item.dc:creator: Debarghya Sil
