item.content:encoded:
Listed eyewear company Lenskart reported a 124.7% jump in its consolidated net profit to ₹232.5 Cr in the September quarter of FY27 (Q2 FY27) from ₹103.5 Cr in the year-ago period, with revenue growth outpacing the increase in expenses.

Operating revenue rose 35.7% to ₹2,845 Cr from ₹2,096.1 Cr in Q2 FY26.

Sequentially, net profit increased 1.8% from ₹228.4 Cr in the preceding quarter, while operating revenue grew 4.8% from ₹2,714.2 Cr.

Including other income of ₹54.5 Cr, Lenskart’s total income stood at ₹2,899.5 Cr during the quarter, compared with ₹2,129.4 Cr a year earlier.

Lenskart’s total expenses increased 31.1% to ₹2,596.8 Cr from ₹1,980.3 Cr in the year-ago quarter.

Lenskart’s India business reported revenue of ₹1,667.9 Cr, up 35.5% from ₹1,230.6 Cr in the year-ago quarter. Its segment profit increased to ₹208.4 Cr from ₹126.1 Cr.

International revenue rose 36.5% to ₹1,201.1 Cr from ₹879.6 Cr, while segment profit more than tripled to ₹97.2 Cr from ₹31.1 Cr.

Lenskart’s EBITDA increased 46.6% YoY to ₹624 Cr during the quarter, with an EBITDA margin of 21.9%. On a pre-Ind AS 116 basis, EBITDA stood at ₹394 Cr, reflecting a 21.9% increase in the company’s operating profitability.

For the first half of the fiscal, Lenskart’s consolidated profit rose 57% YoY to ₹319.3 Cr while operating revenue rose 33% to ₹3,188 Cr.

Lenskart’s Q2 Operational Update 

The company continued to expand its retail footprint, adding 165 net new stores during Q2 FY27, taking its total active store count in India to 2,868 and international stores to 756. Of the new additions, 143 stores were in India and 22 were overseas.

This expansion is covered by its operating cash flow, the company said. Operating cash flow for the quarter stood at ₹388 Cr while capital expenditure on stores, refurbishments and remote optometry was ₹187 Cr. Further, its return on capital employed improved to 22.5% in H1 FY27 from 14.6% in FY26.

Its India business recorded same-store sales growth (SSSG) of 20.8%, while sales per store growth (SPSG) stood at 27.1%. The company also conducted 70 Lakh eye tests in India during the quarter, up 44.1% YoY, while eyewear units sold increased 26.5% to 86 Lakh.

Internationally, eyewear units sold grew 29.7% YoY to 20.6 Lakh, while eye tests increased 15% to 8.4 Lakh.

Meanwhile, Lenskart’s active Gold membership base in India crossed 1 Cr in H1 FY27, up from 90 Lakh in FY26. 

On the manufacturing front, Lenskart continued to increase its in-house production capabilities. Frames manufactured in-house across India, China and Thailand rose 71.7% YoY to 36 Lakh units in Q2 FY27. In-house lens manufacturing increased 52.2% to 20 Lakh units.

The company is also developing a centralised manufacturing facility in Hyderabad as part of its efforts to strengthen its manufacturing and supply chain capabilities.

Shares of Lenskart ended today’s trading session rose 2.97% to ₹691.

item.title: MapmyIndia Q2: Profit Rises 90% YoY To ₹35 Cr, Revenue Up 16%
item.dc:creator: Akshit Pushkarna

item.content:encoded:
MapmyIndia reported a 90.6% YoY jump in its consolidated net profit for the September quarter (Q2 FY27) to ₹35.3 Cr from ₹18.5 Cr in the year-ago period. Sequentially, the profit declined 29.1% from ₹49.7 Cr in the preceding quarter.

Operating revenue rose 15.8% to ₹131.7 Cr during the quarter from ₹113.8 Cr in Q2 FY26. The top line declined 5.7% sequentially from ₹139.7 Cr. 

Total income, including other income of ₹16.1 Cr, increased 19.1% to ₹147.9 Cr from ₹124.2 Cr in the year-ago period.

The company’s EBITDA increased 60.1% YoY to ₹45 Cr, while EBITDA margin expanded to 34.1% from 24.7% in Q2 FY26. PAT margin also improved to 23.8% from 14.9% in the corresponding quarter last year.

For the first half of FY27 (H1 FY27), operating revenue grew 18.4% YoY to ₹271.5 Cr, while EBITDA increased 20.4% to ₹101.1 Cr. Net profit rose 32.2% to ₹85 Cr from ₹64.3 Cr in H1 FY26. 

Automotive, Enterprise Businesses Drive Growth

Commenting on the performance, CMD Rakesh Verma said the company’s automotive business recorded 51.9% YoY growth in Q2 FY27, while its enterprise business grew 44.1%. For H1 FY27, the two verticals recorded growth of 40.4% and 16.5%, respectively.

The automotive business’ performance was driven by increasing adoption of the company’s integrated map-led and IoT-led mobility solutions, Verma said.

From a product perspective, map-led revenue grew 8.9% to ₹175.3 Cr in H1 FY27, while EBITDA margins for the business stood at 47.1%. IoT-led revenue increased 29.1% to ₹96.2 Cr during the period.

The IoT-led business also reported a significant improvement in profitability, with EBITDA increasing to ₹18.5 Cr in H1 FY27 from ₹7.9 Cr in the corresponding period last year. The company attributed this to higher-margin solutions and operating leverage.

MapmyIndia provides digital map data, geospatial software and location-based IoT products, platforms and solutions. Its offerings include mapping APIs, navigation and telematics solutions for automotive and enterprise customers.

MapmyIndia Rejigs Leadership 

Alongside its Q2 results, MapmyIndia announced a series of leadership changes across its technology, product and business teams as it looks to expand its AI capabilities and develop new products.

The company appointed Abhit Kalasotra as chief technology officer (CTO), software engineering, and Nitin Sagar as chief product technology officer (CPTO) for Mappls AI, effective November 4, 2026.

Kalasotra brings over 22 years of technical experience, including 12 years of building technology companies. He has previously worked with Microsoft, Nokia, Emuzed, LG and Motorola. He holds a bachelor’s degree in computer science from BITS Pilani.

Sagar, meanwhile, has over 17 years of experience across location intelligence, digital payments and global travel. He previously worked at MapmyIndia between 2009 and 2015, where he led product and platform development and integrations with automotive manufacturers. 

The company also re-designated Rashmi Verma, previously CTO and chief human resource officer (CHRO), as chief innovation officer (CIO). In her new role, she will focus on driving innovation and accelerating the adoption of AI and emerging technologies across the group.

Separately, CFO Anuj Kumar Jain has been assigned the additional responsibility of chief operating officer (COO) at Gtropy Systems Private Limited, a subsidiary of MapmyIndia. Vishal Pandey has also been appointed chief business officer (CBO) of Gtropy Systems, with both changes taking effect on November 4.

The leadership changes come as MapmyIndia looks to embed AI, machine learning and neural networks across its map-led and IoT-led platforms. These applications span intelligent mapping, navigation, in-vehicle intelligence, telematics, analytics and workflow automation.

Verma said the company sees long-term growth opportunities across its market and product segments, backed by its proprietary data, geospatial capabilities and IoT portfolio.

Shares of MapmyIndia ended today’s trading session 4.57% higher at ₹890.20 apiece on the BSE.

item.title: Pine Labs Partners With Stripe To Unify Online, In-Store Payments In Singapore
item.dc:creator: Anne Florentyna
item.description: Listed fintech major Pine Labs has partnered with global payments infrastructure provider Stripe to launch a solution that allows eligible…
item.content:encoded:
Listed fintech major Pine Labs has partnered with global payments infrastructure provider Stripe to launch a solution that allows eligible retailers in Singapore to manage online and in-store payments through a single platform.

The offering combines Stripe’s online payment capabilities with Pine Labs’ payment terminals and merchant commerce tools. Participating merchants will be able to process online payments through Stripe and accept card payments at physical stores through Pine Labs’ terminals, starting this month.

The companies plan to expand the offering to other Southeast Asian markets in 2027.

The solution targets retailers selling through both physical stores and digital channels. Managing separate payment providers across these channels can complicate reporting and reconciliation, while adding to operational costs.

Beyond payment acceptance, retailers will get access to Pine Labs’ instalment plans from multiple issuers, loyalty-linked payments, pay-by-points options, merchant-funded promotions, and digital marketing tools.

The companies will showcase the solution at the Singapore Fintech Festival 2026.

Pine Labs’ Overseas Push

The partnership builds on Pine Labs’ expansion of its merchant payments and commerce business across international markets.

As of Q2 FY27, Pine Labs served 11.6 Lakh merchants, up 13% YoY, with a presence across more than 22 markets. Its offerings span merchant payments, payment orchestration, issuing, prepaid instruments, and credit infrastructure, with acquisitions helping broaden its product portfolio.

Pine Labs merged its Singapore holding company with its Indian entity in June 2025. It subsequently listed on the BSE and the NSE at ₹242 apiece, a 9.5% premium to its issue price.

On the financial front, Pine Labs’ net profit jumped more than sixfold to ₹38.6 Cr in Q2 FY27 from ₹6 Cr in the year-ago quarter. Operating revenue rose 24% YoY to ₹806.2 Cr.

Shares of Pine Labs were trading 1.15% higher at ₹157.70 apiece on the BSE at 14:45 IST.

item.title: Jio In Talks With US-Based Comcast, Charter To License Broadband Technology: Report
item.dc:creator: Shrishti Bisht
item.description: Recently listed Jio Platforms has held discussions with US cable operators Comcast and Charter Communications about licensing its wireless broadband…
item.content:encoded:
Recently listed Jio Platforms has held discussions with US cable operators Comcast and Charter Communications about licensing its wireless broadband technology in exchange for potential equity stakes.

According to a Reuters report, the discussions are part of the Reliance Industries-controlled company’s overseas expansion plans, centred on selling its proprietary unlicensed band radio (UBR) technology to foreign operators rather than building networks abroad.

Jio is targeting 10-15 global partners for the technology, which delivers high-speed internet to buildings without requiring cable connections to individual homes.

However, there is no timeline for reaching an agreement with any of the companies it has approached, the report said.

Jio also held discussions with South Africa’s MTN Group, but the talks fell through after the two sides failed to agree on valuation and certain licensing issues. The report cited one of the sources as saying that MTN could not persuade Jio to invest at a valuation acceptable to the Indian company.

Inc42 has reached out to Jio Platforms, Comcast and Charter Communications for comments on the development. The story will be updated on receiving their responses.

Jio Eyes Overseas Markets For UBR Technology

Jio’s UBR platform operates on free, unlicensed Wi-Fi frequencies. It uses transmitters installed on nearby towers or rooftops to beam internet to receivers fitted on buildings.

The technology could help operators deliver broadband without laying cables to individual homes or relying on licensed mobile spectrum. Reliance has described it as a global first.

A partnership with Comcast or Charter could give Jio access to the US residential broadband market, where cable operators are facing growing competition from fibre and fixed wireless services.

Comcast had around 28.3 Mn residential broadband customers at the end of September, while Charter had approximately 29.4 Mn internet customers in June. Both companies have been losing customers to fixed wireless and fibre providers.

Last month, Jio made its stock market debut following a $3.2 Bn IPO, listing at a 21.36% premium to the issue price of ₹1,119 on BSE and NSE.

Jio Platforms reported a net profit of ₹8,387 Cr in Q2 FY27, up 13.7% from ₹7,375 Cr in the year-ago quarter. Sequentially, profit rose 8% from ₹7,764 Cr.

During its earnings call, Jio Platforms MD Akash Ambani said the company wanted to take UBR to both developed and developing markets but would be selective about where it expands.

“We want to be a technology-led business there,” he said, highlighting the potential of the US market.

Jio added 9.1 Mn customers on a net basis during the quarter, taking its subscriber base to 542.4 Mn. It also reported 300 Mn 5G subscribers.

item.title: Freshworks Swings To $18 Mn Profit In Q3, Revenue Rises 14% YoY To $245 Mn
item.dc:creator: Anjali Jain
item.description: Nasdaq-listed SaaS company Freshworks swung to a consolidated net profit of $18.3 Mn in the third quarter of 2026 (Q3…
item.content:encoded:
Nasdaq-listed SaaS company Freshworks swung to a consolidated net profit of $18.3 Mn in the third quarter of 2026 (Q3 2026) from a $4.7 Mn loss a year earlier, helped by higher revenue and lower operating expenses.

Revenue rose 14% to $245.4 Mn from $215.1 Mn in the corresponding quarter last year.

Sequentially, revenue increased 3.4% from $237.4 Mn, while net profit rose from $3.2 Mn.

The company’s operating expenses declined 4.4% to $181.2 Mn from $189.6 Mn. General and administrative expenses fell to $38.2 Mn from $47.1 Mn, while stock-based compensation dropped to $38.8 Mn from $48.5 Mn.

Enterprise Push Gains Traction

CEO Dennis Woodside said Freshworks’ strategy of targeting larger customers supported its quarterly performance. New deals involving multiple employee experience products increased more than 35%, while partners participated in more than half of its new business, he said.

The number of customers contributing over $100,000 in annual recurring revenue (ARR) increased 25% to 1,821. Customers generating more than $50,000 in ARR grew 18% to 4,257.

Freshworks also crossed $1 Bn in ARR after the quarter ended, ahead of its earlier year-end target.

However, its net dollar retention (NDR) rate remained unchanged sequentially at 104%, down from 105% a year earlier. NDR measures changes in revenue from existing customers, accounting for upgrades, cross-sells, renewals, and customer churn.

New customers during the quarter included Tata Technologies, Texas Christian University, Unilabs (UK), and Jose Cuervo.

Freshworks has been increasingly positioning itself as an AI-powered service operations platform spanning customer experience, employee experience, and IT service management.

Freshworks Raises Full-Year Outlook

For the fourth quarter of 2026, Freshworks expects revenue of $253.5 Mn and $254.5 Mn, representing approximately 14% growth.

It forecast full-year revenue of $965 Mn-$966 Mn implying about 15% growth. This narrows its earlier guidance of $963.5 Mn-$966.5 Mn. 

Founded in 2010 by Girish Mathrubootham and Shan Krishnasamy, Freshworks offers cloud-based software for customer support, sales automation, and IT service management. It became the first Indian SaaS company to list on Nasdaq in September 2021.

Under Woodside, who succeeded Mathrubootham as CEO in 2024, the company has sharpened its focus on AI-led enterprise software.

In May 2026, Freshworks announced plans to cut approximately 500 jobs, or 11% of its workforce, to realign operations around its growth priorities and accelerate its AI push.

It has also expanded through acquisitions, buying IT incident management platform FireHydrant for $88.7 Mn in cash in January to strengthen its IT service and operations portfolio.

More recently, Freshworks acquired Israel-based AI startup Robusta Dev for an undisclosed amount. It plans to integrate Robusta’s AI-powered outage investigation and corrective recommendations into Freshservice, complementing FireHydrant’s incident response tools.
